q: Why was the worst day so bad?
answer:
Net profit on 2026-10-09 was ₹-26,445 — about ₹9,734 worse than its usual same‑weekday level (usual: ₹-16,711, a 58.3% drop). The data shows the day was worse because margin and sales moved against profit, not because of a single verified external cause.

- What changed (size and why it matters)
  - Net profit: 2026-10-09 = ₹-26,445 vs usual same‑weekday ≈ ₹-16,711 (worse by ₹9,734). This is a notable negative swing in profit.
  - Net sales (P&L basis): ₹53,880 on 2026-10-09, down from a prior-day reference of ₹90,962 (−40.8%). Lower revenue removed the top‑line cushion for profit.
  - Ad spend (P&L basis): ₹60,102 on 2026-10-09 (vs ₹69,851 on 2026-10-08). Higher-than-usual ad cost relative to the sales it bought increased the loss: the change in ad spend accounted for ~82% of the net profit move in the decomposition the analysis produced.
  - Contribution margin dropped: contribution margin fell to ₹33,657 (from ₹51,303 the previous day), explaining much of the net profit decline.
- Where the change sat
  - The deterioration concentrated in specific campaigns/ads (examples flagged in the analysis include campaign TH-383-SUSPENDER-29SEP and a small set of ads that together moved several thousand rupees of profit that day). These campaign-level swings explain a material share of the profit change versus the usual weekday.
- Did we identify a cause?
  - No single upstream cause met the statistical bar. The diagnosis is arithmetic: lower sales plus the pattern of ad spend and campaign-level performance produced the loss. The engine did not label any external event (inventory, refunds, booking timing, or a single campaign edit) as a supported cause.

Worth checking:
- Break this day down by ad campaign and ad creative (the flagged campaigns show the largest negative swings).
- Compare order volume and conversion rates for those campaigns on 2026-10-09 vs the usual same weekday to see if reduced conversion or poor-performing creatives explain the revenue drop.
- Reconcile P&L ad allocation for the flagged campaigns to confirm whether spend was concentrated but delivered low credited sales.
